title: Deuterium and Water - The Heavy Hydrogen Problem
summary: Start here for Water: what deuterium is, why life prefers light hydrogen, how Dr. Jack Kruse links a weakening magnetic field and the Van Allen belts to rising deuterium in water — and why the water your mitochondria make matters more than the water you drink.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body: Albert Szent-Györgyi — who won the Nobel Prize for discovering vitamin C — put it simply: "We live by a small trickle of electricity from the sun." Plants harvest sunlight into food; we eat it, strip the hydrogen off that food, and turn its electrons into ATP, the energy that runs every cell. This lesson is about one detail hiding inside "hydrogen" and "water" that Dr. Jack Kruse argues is central to health: not all hydrogen is the same, and the heavy kind, known as deuterium, quietly throttles your cellular engines.

sections.heading: Protium vs Deuterium
sections.body: Ordinary hydrogen (also called protium) is a single proton with one electron. Deuterium is hydrogen with a neutron added, so it is slightly more than twice as heavy and physically larger. That extra mass is not trivial as thhe mass changes bond lengths, bond strength, and how easily a particle can "quantum tunnel" through the tiny channels cells use. Life runs on tunneling light protons. Anything the size of a proton or bigger faces a higher energy barrier. So biology has several reasons to favour light hydrogen and to actively push deuterium out. Heavy water and your cells are like oil and water.

sections.heading: Mitochondria and ATP Synthase
sections.body: Your mitochondria strip hydrogen from food, pull the electrons off, and pack the bare protons into the mitochondrial matrix. Those protons then flood back through ATP synthase, the smallest rotary motor in nature, which spins at roughly 9,000 rpm to make ATP. That motor was built to accept a lone proton, not a proton-plus-neutron. Feed it deuterium and the heavier, bulkier ion changes the viscosity and can't move through cleanly, so the motor drops well below 100% efficiency and makes less ATP. This is the mechanistic reason deuterium-depleted water (DDW) improves mitochondrial function in lab and animal studies, and a big part of why Kruse argues cancer is fundamentally a mitochondrial problem, not a genetic one.

sections.heading: EZ Water, Charge, and the Cell's Battery
sections.body: When sunlight hits the water in a cell, it builds coherent, structured layers called exclusion-zone (EZ) water that liberate protons and exclude anything proton-sized or larger. EZ water is a liquid-crystalline battery: bigger EZ means more separated charge, which means a higher redox potential, or more work the cell can do. Because deuterium is heavier and carries charge poorly, water loaded with it forms a weaker EZ and stores less charge. In Kruse's framing, at cell scale the electrostatic force dominates and gravity is negligible, so this charge/battery function is what really governs a cell's energy, and deuterium quietly drains it.

sections.heading: Deuterium amd the Van Allen belts
sections.body: This is where Water meets the Magnetism pillar. As we go through a magnetic excursion, Earth's magnetic field is weakening, and as it does the Van Allen radiation belts dip closer to the surface. This can be seen most dramatically over an area refered to as the South Atlantic Anomaly. Kruse argues that this lets rain and surface water pick up more deuterium over time, raising the isotopic load in the nearby water sources. Thus, sourcing water from naturally occurring sources with low deuterium content, such as deep in the ground/primary water sources, may be important to combat the increased deuterium caused by the weakening magnetic field.

sections.heading: Lattice Lock
sections.body: Kruse describes a failure mode he calls lattice lock. Your body normally fractionates hydrogen isotopes, sorting light protium from heavy deuterium in your blood stream. If you're flooded with deuterium and cut off from the natural magnetic reference, that sorting fails. The internal water lattice collapses from a structured state, the EZ battery weakens, ATP synthase bogs down, and oxygen is more likely to tip from its safe triplet state into the damaging singlet state. In his model this stalled, non-fractionating state is where chronic disease takes hold.

sections.heading: What to do Daily
sections.body: The most important point is that the water that matters most is the water your mitochondria make. Burning fat (beta-oxidation) and running clean metabolism generate deuterium-depleted water inside the cell, and only that internal water, hit by sunlight, forms the EZ. The water you drink mainly serves the fluid around cells. Be sure to get strong morning and midday light, favour lower-deuterium foods (cold-water seafood, quality fats, C3 plants over corn/cane sugar), finish eating earlier, ground to the Earth, and protect dark low-EMF nights. For drinking water, choose clean sources free of fluoride, bromine, glyphosate and heavy metals. Icelandic glacial spring water and water sourced from deep/primary water tables tend to be lower in deuterium. Deuterium-depleted water is a more advanced and costly option.
